story: A prophet known as the Great Peacemaker (also called Deganawida) arose among the Native peoples of the northeast woodlands. Some said he was born to a Huron mother as a virgin birth; others said he was born Onondaga and later adopted by the Mohawk. He traveled from settlement to settlement announcing that he came from the west, going east, to spread peace so that the shedding of blood might cease. His first ally was a woman called Jigonhsasee, who became known as the Mother of Nations; she lent her home for meetings of rival tribal leaders and advised him which leaders to approach. His follower Hiawatha, an Onondaga famed for oratory, helped him win the tribes to his vision. When the Mohawk at first rejected his message, the Peacemaker climbed a tree above a great waterfall and had warriors chop it down; he vanished into the rapids below and was presumed dead, but was found alive by a campfire the next morning. Impressed, the Mohawk became the founding tribe of a confederacy of tribes. The assembled tribes gathered at a lake, planted a Tree of Peace, and proclaimed a Great Binding Law. He also walked upon a great lake, possessed a canoe that could fly, and traveled healing the sick. He established a council of chiefs, with power shared between men and women in a matrilineal system, women able to depose unfit chiefs. He prophesied that a white serpent would befriend his people then betray them, a red serpent would fight it, a chosen boy would be given great power, and finally a black serpent would defeat both, until a blinding light—himself—ended the conflict and his people accepted the white serpent as a long-lost brother.

Some said he was born to a mother of one people as a virgin birth; others said he was born into a second people and later adopted by a third. He traveled from settlement to settlement announcing that he came from the west, going east, to spread peace so that the shedding of blood might cease. When one tribe at first rejected his message, the peacemaker climbed a tree above a great waterfall and had warriors chop it down; he vanished into the rapids below and was presumed dead, but was found alive by a campfire the next morning. Impressed, that tribe became the founding tribe of a confederacy of tribes. The assembled tribes gathered at a lake, planted a tree symbolizing peace, and proclaimed a binding law. He also walked upon a great lake, possessed a canoe that could fly, and traveled healing the sick. He established a council of chiefs, with power shared between men and women in a matrilineal system, women able to depose unfit chiefs. title: Great Peacemaker
